sections.prepared_remarks: Tesla Q1 revenue $21.3 billion, down 9 percent year over year due to declining vehicle ASPs and lower delivery volumes. We delivered 386,000 vehicles, down 8 percent year over year. Auto gross margin excluding credits was 16.3 percent, down from 18.9 percent a year ago. We are in a difficult period but the foundation for future growth is strong. FSD v12.5 is seeing strong adoption — we are seeing insurance discounts for FSD users in several US states. Robotaxi will launch in Austin in June. We expect regulatory approval in California by Q4. Tesla's energy business is a major growth engine with storage deployments of 9.4 GWh in Q1. Megapack factory in Lathrop is at capacity. Dojo supercomputer is training next-generation FSD models — we now have 3 billion miles of real-world FSD driving data. Our next-generation affordable vehicle platform is targeting $25,000 average selling price with 50 percent cost reduction versus Model 3. Production starts in H2 2025.
sections.financial_highlights: Revenue $21.3 billion, EPS $0.39, gross margin 17.4 percent. Energy revenue $2.7 billion, up 67 percent. Services revenue $2.9 billion, up 22 percent. We continue to generate free cash flow of $1.2 billion despite margin pressure. We are executing $2 billion cost reduction program across manufacturing and supply chain. Our Austin gigafactory is producing Model Y with new structural battery pack at significantly lower cost. Deferred revenue from FSD subscriptions reached $1.9 billion. We expect volume growth to resume in Q2 as new model launches ramp. H2 2025 will see five new products including the affordable EV, next-gen Roadster, and Cybercab. We are targeting 30 percent gross margin within 18 months.
sections.qanda_session:
Levy Germ: Elon, robotaxi in Austin — can you help us understand the regulatory path? You've said June, but are you assuming a federal framework or state-by-state approvals? And how many vehicles will be in the initial fleet?

Elon Musk: Levy, we're launching with the Texas Public Utilities Commission approval which we already have. The initial fleet is 10 to 20 vehicles in Austin, limited geofenced areas, expanding to 1,000 vehicles by end of year. California approval is expected Q4 — the DMV process is progressing well. The Cybercab, our purpose-built robotaxi, will enter production at the end of 2026 with a cost under $25,000 per unit. The economics are extraordinary: a Cybercab operating 16 hours per day at $0.30 per mile generates $50,000 to $100,000 annual revenue per vehicle after energy and maintenance costs. The capital efficiency of operating instead of selling vehicles is transformational for Tesla's revenue model. We expect robotic taxi revenue to exceed automotive revenue within five years.

Rod Lache: Vaibhav, on the cost reduction program — you've guided to 50 percent cost reduction on the next-gen platform, but you've also said you're 40 percent through in the current program. Where specifically are you seeing the biggest breakthroughs? And does the $25,000 price point imply you are comfortable with near-zero margins on the entry-level vehicle?

Vaibhav Taneja: Rod, the cost reduction is coming from three areas: manufacturing innovation like the unboxed assembly process, battery pack redesign to cut cell costs 30 percent, and supply chain renegotiation. The current program is delivering roughly $2,000 to $2,500 in savings per vehicle versus the Model 3 baseline. On the $25,000 vehicle: we expect low-single-digit gross margins at launch, scaling to 15 to 20 percent within 18 months of volume production. Tesla has always been willing to take near-zero margin vehicles that grow the fleet and enable FSD data collection and energy ecosystem attachment. The lifetime value of each vehicle is what matters, not the initial margin. We expect energy attachment rates of 40 percent and FSD subscription penetration of 25 percent on the affordable platform.
sections.forward_outlook: Elon Musk: Tesla is three businesses in one — electric vehicles, energy storage, and artificial intelligence. The market is underestimating all three. Our AI advantage is real and compounding: 3 billion miles of supervised FSD data, Dojo training, and the robotaxi network creates a data moat that no competitor can replicate quickly. The energy business grows 60 to 70 percent year over year — Megapack is sold out through 2026. We are scaling Powerwall for residential to capture the home backup and virtual power plant opportunity. Over the next 18 months, Tesla will launch five new vehicles. This is the most prolific product launch period in Tesla's history.
